1. Query the atlas

Source: vignettes/query_the_atlas.Rmd
query_the_atlas.Rmd

Source: vignettes/query_the_atlas.Rmd

This practice takes Human Cell Atlas data from CELLxGENE. Each study is a table of measurements at single cell level (one row per cell). cellNexus makes that query reusable and fast at the sample level. It also adds three cell-type labels with SingleR, using the Blueprint, Monaco, and Azimuth references. A harmonisation step then combines those three labels into one unified cell-type label for every cell. The diagram below shows the preprocessing steps, starting from the original CELLxGENE data.

Setup 

library(cellNexus)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

get_metadata() returns a lazy DuckDB table, and accepts tidyverse syntax to filter the data.

Quality control

  • An empty droplet is liquid captured with almost no cell in it. It still produces a few gene measurements, mostly background. Counting it as a cell inflates the number of cells and adds noise.
  • A dead cell is detected by a high mitochondrial percentage.
  • A doublet is two cells captured together. Their measurements are mixed, so the row can look like a cell type that does not exist.
metadata <- get_metadata() |>
  keep_quality_cells()

metadata

keep_quality_cells() applies one gate and filters out bad quality cells from every sample. This is a filter shortcut, which is equivalent to directly applying three filters to each sample: empty_droplet == FALSE, alive == TRUE, scDblFinder.class != "doublet".

The same checks are computed for each sample. Detailed technical information on the quality-control procedure is available in the cellNexus quality-control steps page.

Choose cells by cell type

cell_type_unified_ensemble is the harmonised label (multi-reference consensus annotation). age_days and imputed_ethnicity are sample-level fields.

Exploring the harmonised cell types in the atlas.

metadata |>
  dplyr::distinct(cell_type_unified_ensemble) |>
  dplyr::arrange(cell_type_unified_ensemble)

Exercise 1. Count cells per cell_type_unified_ensemble for donors older than 50 years (age_days > 50 * 365). Which labels are rare enough that a proportion estimated from 50 cells would be mostly sampling noise?

Solution 
library(cellNexus)
library(dplyr)

get_metadata() |>
  keep_quality_cells() |>
  dplyr::filter(age_days > 50 * 365) |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, sort = TRUE)

A label with a few dozen cells across the whole atlas will have a very wide composition interval. Drop it from the cell-type list, or accept that its estimate is descriptive.

This case study uses nine respiratory reference studies. Each study has a unique dataset_id.

dataset_ids <- c(
  "9f222629-9e39-47d0-b83f-e08d610c7479",

Query metadata by tissue

get_metadata() does not carry original CELLxGENE annotations such as tissue, disease, sex, assay, cell_type, and self_reported_ethnicity. Join those columns onto get_metadata().

The file below is the CELLxGENE Census obs table for snapshot 2024-07-01, limited to these nine studies and to the columns this join uses. cellxgene.census does not run on Windows, so the workshop reads this parquet instead of opening the Census.

duckdb_register_arrow() makes the Arrow table visible to the same DuckDB connection as metadata, so the join stays lazy.

census_metadata <- cellNexus::get_census_metadata("2024-07-01")
con <- dbplyr::remote_con(metadata)
duckdb::duckdb_register_arrow(con, "census_metadata", census_metadata)

metadata_respiratory <- metadata |>
  dplyr::filter(dataset_id %in% dataset_ids) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::tbl(con, "census_metadata") |>
      dplyr::select(
        observation_joinid, dataset_id, tissue,
        self_reported_ethnicity, cell_type, assay,
        disease, sex
      ),
    by = c("observation_joinid", "dataset_id")
  )

metadata_respiratory |>
  dplyr::count(tissue, sort = TRUE)

Since cellxgene.census does not run on Windows, the workshop reads this parquet instead of opening the Census. Read the parquet as a data frame and join back to the metadata.

census_metadata <- arrow::read_parquet(
  system.file(
    "extdata",
    "census_respiratory_2024-07-01.parquet",
    package = "cellNexusWorkshop"
  )
)

metadata_respiratory <- metadata |>
  dplyr::filter(dataset_id %in% dataset_ids) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    census_metadata |>
      dplyr::select(
        observation_joinid, dataset_id, tissue,
        self_reported_ethnicity, cell_type, assay,
        disease, sex
      ),
    by = c("observation_joinid", "dataset_id"),
    copy = TRUE
  )

metadata_respiratory |>
  dplyr::count(tissue, sort = TRUE)

Build the respiratory ageing cohort

This step keeps immune and epithelial labels, lung and airway tissues, and donors from 1 year up to 80 years.

dplyr::collect() runs the query. dataset_id is rewritten with underscores because a hyphenated UUID is not a legal name in a model formula. age_years, age_binary, and age_bin are derived here so the composition model and the expression model use the same donors. Samples with fewer than 50 cells are dropped, and duplicate observation_joinid rows are removed. Every cell of every retained sample is kept. sccomp conditions on each sample’s total, and the expression model carries library size as a covariate, so equal-size subsampling would throw away precision.

respiratory_tissues <- c(
  "lung", "lung parenchyma", "alveolus of lung", "bronchus",
  "respiratory airway", "pleura", "pleural effusion",
  "middle lobe of right lung", "upper lobe of left lung",
  "lower lobe of left lung", "upper lobe of right lung",
  "lower lobe of right lung", "lingula of left lung",
  "right lung", "left lung"
)

immune_cell_types <- c(
  "cd16 mono", "nk", "mait", "cd14 mono", "cdc", "b memory", "pdc",
  "nkt", "cd4 th1/th17 em", "plasma", "cd4 th17 em", "b naive", "macrophage",
  "cd4 th2 em", "cd8 tcm", "cd8 naive", "cd8 tem", "tgd", "cd4 fh em",
  "cd4 th1 em", "cd4 tem", "cd4 naive", "mast", "treg", "cd4 tcm", "granulocyte"
)
epithelial_cell_types <- c("epithelial", "pneumocyte", "secretory")
cell_types_query <- c(immune_cell_types, epithelial_cell_types)

obs_lung <- metadata_respiratory |>
  dplyr::filter(
    cell_type_unified_ensemble %in% c(immune_cell_types, epithelial_cell_types),
    tissue %in% respiratory_tissues,
    age_days >= 365,
    age_days < 80 * 365
  ) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample_id = as.character(sample_id),
    dataset_id = gsub("-", "_", as.character(dataset_id), fixed = TRUE),
    age_years = as.numeric(age_days / 365.25),
    age_binary = age_years > 50,
    age_bin = cut(
      age_years,
      breaks = c(0, 50, 80),
      right = FALSE,
      labels = c("20-49", "50-79")
    )
  )

# Drop samples below 50 cells 
obs_lung <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() >= 50, .by = sample_id) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dataset_id, sample_id, observation_joinid) |>
  dplyr::distinct(observation_joinid, .keep_all = TRUE)

age_scaled <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, age_years) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_years_scaled_centered = as.numeric(scale(age_years)[, 1])
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(sample_id, age_years_scaled_centered)

obs_lung <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::left_join(age_scaled, by = "sample_id")

obs_lung |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, name = "n_cells") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_cells))
## # A tibble: 29 × 2

age_binary is TRUE for donors older than 50 years. age_bin is the same split, labelled for plots. One encoding means the composition model and the expression model contrast the same donors. The boundary is a modelling choice: report it, and check that both sides are populated.

Inspect the cohort before modelling

Look at the age histogram and the cell-type bar chart before fitting a model. Both age classes should contain donors. Ages clumped into two distant groups will make a continuous age slope rest on whichever studies sit at the extremes. A cell type with only a handful of cells will have an uninformative composition interval.

p_age <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, age_years) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_years)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Samples")

p_types <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, name = "n_cells") |>
  ggplot(aes(cell_type_unified_ensemble, n_cells)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cells")

p_age + p_types & theme_bw()

Exercise 2. How many distinct samples fall in each age_bin?

Solution 
obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, age_bin) |>
  dplyr::count(age_bin)

Both bins should contain donors. A bin with a handful of samples cannot support the age term once dataset_id is in the model.

Exercise 3. Cross-tabulate distinct samples by dataset_id and age_binary. Which studies contain donors of both age classes? A study that contains only one class cannot separate age from study, and both models below include dataset_id.

Solution 
obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, dataset_id, age_binary) |>
  dplyr::count(dataset_id, age_binary) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = age_binary, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

A study with a zero in either age class does not identify an age effect on its own. The fixed dataset_id term uses the studies that contain both classes.
